subject: Communication
title: Emotional Contagion: Catching Feelings
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Emotional Contagion: Catching Feelings.

hook.text: One anxious person enters a calm meeting. Ten minutes later, everyone's on edge. Nobody knows why.

buildup.text: Emotional contagion is the unconscious transfer of moods between people — through facial mimicry, tone, and posture.

discovery.text: Hatfield's research shows we automatically mimic expressions of people we interact with — within 50 milliseconds.

twist.text: Leaders are 'super-spreaders' of emotion. A leader's mood disproportionately affects the entire team's emotional climate.

climax.text: Emotional intelligence includes managing what you broadcast — because your emotions don't stay with you.

punchline.text: Your mood isn't personal. It's contagious.

quiz.question: How quickly do people begin mimicking others' facial expressions?

details.summary: Emotional contagion is the automatic transfer of emotions between people through facial expressions, tone, posture, and neurological mirroring. It happens in milliseconds without conscious awareness. Leaders' emotions spread most powerfully because attention flows upward in hierarchies.
details.whyItMatters: Your emotions literally infect the people around you. Leaders who manage their emotional state manage their team's performance.
takeaways: Emotions transfer automatically through nonverbal channels
Contagion happens in milliseconds below conscious awareness
Leaders' emotions spread most powerfully through hierarchies

faq.question: Can negative emotions spread through a whole organization?
faq.answer: Yes. Research shows that a single angry or anxious leader can shift an entire team's emotional tone within minutes. Over time, chronic negativity from leadership creates a toxic emotional climate that affects recruitment, retention, and productivity across the organization.

faq.question: How do you protect yourself from negative emotional contagion?
faq.answer: Awareness is the first defense. Notice when your mood shifts after interacting with someone. Develop centering practices like deep breathing. Limit exposure to chronically negative people. After unavoidable negative exposure, deliberately engage with positive people to reset your state.
